title: request-morphology-lab-notes-and-prioritization-2026-11-15
content:
Executive snapshot:
This is a working synthesis from the last 3 weeks of CS intake, field interviews, and ticket triage. Goal: convert high-signal yet messy request threads into a short list of low-effort probes + two mid-scope projects to surface in next sprint planning. Not polished — notes, rough quotes, and proposed tiny experiments included.

How to use this doc (quick):
- Read the 3 prioritized clusters below (Morph A/B/C).
- Each cluster has: raw quotes, hypothesis, low-effort probe, estimated dev effort (T-shirt), priority score (impact x pain / effort), and suggested owner.
- At bottom: monitoring/acceptance criteria and next steps (timeboxed).

Intake sources summarized:
- Support tickets (JIRA-3421, JIRA-3499) — 18 unique customers mentioning degraded output during model fallbacks or cost spikes.
- Customer calls (Enterprise: FinRegCo, HealthSynth, EdgeAI startup) — demos + pain stories.
- Slack threads (#cs-field-signal, #eng-runtime) and two GitHub issues calling for a KV-cache inspection UI.

Raw customer snippets (verbatim-ish):
- "When large requests hit, we see the model silently drop to a smaller variant and outputs go weird. No visibility — we only notice when users complain." — FinRegCo product lead
- "We pay for tokens across retries; when fallback happens, it looks like doubled spend. Need cost clarity per route." — EdgeAI platform engineer
- "Our on-prem instance loses KV context occasionally during autoscale bursts. Devs need a way to snapshot/inspect caches." — HealthSynth SRE

Cluster Morph A: graceful fallbacks and per-route cost transparency
- Problem statement: customers experience silent model variant fallbacks (CPU/GPU/quantized), which causes quality regressions and unclear cost attribution.
- Hypothesis: adding explicit fallback logs + a per-request cost breakdown will reduce support incidents and time-to-detect by 60%.
- Low-effort probe (quick):
  - Add a single-line header in response metadata: "served_variant:" and "fallback_reason:" for the next 2 weeks for hosted API only (feature flagged).
  - Also enable a debug query param (?debug=serve_trace=1) to return a compact cost-breakdown array: [model_variant, tokens_charged, estimate_usd].
- Acceptance / metrics:
  - Reduction in fallback-related support tickets by 50% in two weeks.
  - 80% of CS triage calls include the header when customers reproduce.
- Rough effort: Small (1-2 sprint days infra change + 1 backend engineer).
- Priority score: High. Suggested owner: Marcus Chen (eng-console-and-tooling).
- Risks: exposing internal variant names might be confusing — document mapping in Console to human labels.

Cluster Morph B: KV-cache visibility and snapshot tooling for private deployments
- Problem: on-prem / VPC customers report "invisible" KV cache resets after autoscaling; debugging requires deep runtime knowledge.
- Hypothesis: a lightweight KV cache inspector (read-only snapshot + basic stats) will cut debugging time and increase trust for Private customers.
- Low-effort probe:
  - Implement an admin-only endpoint (/admin/kv-inspect) that returns: cache_size, top-n keys by hit_rate, last_eviction_ts, and histogram of segment sizes. Return only metadata (no token/plaintext). Feature-flag and gate behind KMS-provisioned roles.
- Mid-scope extension: UI panel in Console Private with 3 charts (hit-rate, evictions over time, mean-kv-lifespan) and a button to capture a snapshot to S3 for diagnostics.
- Acceptance / metrics:
  - Time-to-diagnose incidents down from median 3 days to <1 day for relevant cases.
  - Positive NPS feedback from HealthSynth pilot (n=3 teams).
- Effort: Probe = Medium (3-5 dev days infra + SRE signoff). UI = Medium-Large (2 sprints).
- Priority: Medium-High for Private customers. Suggested owner: Lina Ortega (solutions-engineering-and-professional-services).
- Compliance notes: snapshots must redact any user content — only return sizes and hashed keys. Coordinate with Security.

Cluster Morph C: token-level cost attribution and retries accounting
- Problem: customers see unexpected token billing when the platform retries or falls back. Billing attribution isn't mapped to retry semantics.
- Hypothesis: providing a token-attribution breakdown per attempt (attempt_1, attempt_2) and linking to request_id will decrease billing disputes and lower churn risk.
- Low-effort probe:
  - Add an additional billing field in usage logs: attempts[] with token_count and variant_name per attempt. Surface a small CSV export from Console for last-30-days route-level attempts.
- Acceptance / metrics:
  - Billing disputes related to retries drop by 70% in 30 days.
  - Finance reports < 5 dispute escalations per month from pilot customers.
- Effort: Small (backend log change + CSV export).
- Priority: High. Suggested owner: Devon Patel (product-hosted-api liaison to finance).

Noise & other asks observed (quick bullets):
- Requests for "predictive autoscaling thresholds by route" (mostly ops teams).
- Want a "model quality baseline" per version — folks ask for canned eval prompts to compare variants.
- More granular quotas (per-team, per-route) and alerting for quota exhaustion events.

Prioritization rubric used (quick):
- Impact = customer reach * severity (1-5)
- Effort = eng estimate (S/M/L)
- Score = impact / effort (simple heuristic used for quick sorting)

Proposed quick roadmap (2-week cadence):
- Sprint 0 (this week): enable feature flags and add metadata headers for fallbacks (Morph A probe). Add a small beta doc in Console help. Owner: Marcus.
- Sprint 1: roll out billing-attribution-attempts and CSV export (Morph C). Finance + billing QA. Owner: Devon.
- Sprint 2–3: KV inspector probe rollout to Private pilot customers (Morph B). Security review + SRE runbook. Owner: Lina.

Acceptance and monitoring (concrete signals):
- New SLI: fallback-header-coverage pct (percent of production responses with serve_trace header when feature-flag on) target 95%.
- Ticket SLO: median time-to-diagnose fallback incidents < 8 hours for pilot customers.
- Billing disputes: tracked in a triage board; aim < 5 escalations/month.

Action items (owner, due):
- Marcus: implement serve_trace header + debug param behind FF (due 2026-11-22).
- Devon: add attempts[] token attribution to usage logs and CSV export (due 2026-11-29). Coordinate with Finance.
- Lina: draft KV-inspect endpoint spec and security redaction plan; identify 3 pilot customers (due 2026-12-03).
- Aditi (owner of this doc): coordinate pilot invites, prepare GH issue templates for eng work, and run a 30-min sync with Finance + SRE next Tue (2026-11-23).

Open questions / discussion points:
- How much internal variant naming is safe to expose in hosted metadata? Need PRD decision.
- For Private, does snapshot retention need to be configurable per-customer? (likely yes due to compliance).
- Should Console map fallback reasons to human-friendly categories (e.g., capacity-shed, seq-too-long, quantized-variant) or keep raw reasons?

Quick experiment hypotheses to A/B test (if we want rapid evidence):
- H1: Exposing serve_trace will reduce time-to-ack on CS calls by 40% because customers can paste header instead of reproducing flow.
- H2: CSV per-route attempts will reduce billing dispute resolution time by 60% because Finance can trivially map charges to attempts.

Notes to self (scrappy bits):
- Draft a short email template for pilot customers explaining what we will log and privacy safeguards.
- Link user-level telemetry to request_id early — that's the glue for debugging across services.
- Slack thread: #cs-field-signal — post a 1-paragraph summary and ask for more verbatim quotes.

Appendix: quick links and references
- JIRA-3421 (support ticket cluster: fallback quality regressions)
- JIRA-3499 (kv-cache stability in private)
- GitHub ops issue: github.com/redwood-inference/ops/issues/128 (KV snapshot S3 ingestion)

End of notes — this doc will be iterated. Keep it rough, call out anything that looks like it belongs to Feature PRD.
